title: Builder Residency Due-Diligence Checklist v1.0
description: An open, machine-readable checklist for verifying dates, operator identity, accommodation, money, work expectations, safety and outcome claims before joining a builder residency.
methodology: Victor Laybats authored the checklist from Crucible CLUB’s public participation methodology and the decision-critical gaps that any cohort-specific offer must resolve. Every item asks for evidence rather than awarding a score. The framework is independent of the status of any current Crucible cohort.
limitations: This is a due-diligence aid, not legal, immigration, tax, medical, insurance or financial advice. It does not verify a venue, operator or cohort and it does not guarantee safety or project outcomes. Time-sensitive details must be checked directly with the organiser and relevant authorities before commitment.

sources.name: Crucible CLUB identity and source hierarchy

criteria.criterion: The legal or responsible operator is named.
criteria.rationale: A participant needs to know who accepts money and carries obligations.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Record the operator name, registration or legal status and service address.

criteria.criterion: A monitored contact and escalation route are provided.
criteria.rationale: Questions and urgent issues need more than a social profile.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Test the ordinary and urgent contact routes.

criteria.criterion: Application status and decision dates are current.
criteria.rationale: An open label can become misleading when dates have passed or a cohort has started.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Capture the page, timestamp and stated decision timeline.

criteria.criterion: Exact arrival, departure and program dates are stated.
criteria.rationale: Travel and accommodation decisions depend on unambiguous dates and time zones.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Record dates, check-in windows and time zone.

criteria.criterion: The city and venue status are confirmed.
criteria.rationale: A concept image or provisional city is not a confirmed accommodation booking.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Request the address or a documented disclosure of when it will be supplied.

criteria.criterion: Room allocation, occupancy and accessibility are described.
criteria.rationale: Shared-room assumptions materially affect fit, privacy and cost.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Record bed type, room sharing, bathrooms, stairs and accessibility constraints.

criteria.criterion: Capacity and minimum viable cohort are disclosed.
criteria.rationale: A residency can change or cancel if too few or too many people join.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Record maximum capacity, minimum cohort and the consequence if unmet.

criteria.criterion: The total price, currency and taxes are stated.
criteria.rationale: A headline price may omit taxes, deposits or mandatory extras.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Request an itemized total in the payment currency.

criteria.criterion: Included and excluded services are itemized.
criteria.rationale: Accommodation, food, transport, workspace and activities should not be inferred.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Create an inclusion and exclusion list.

criteria.criterion: Payment recipient, schedule and method are verifiable.
criteria.rationale: The payee should match the responsible operator or a disclosed agent.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Record invoice issuer, payee, due dates and payment protection.

criteria.criterion: Cancellation, refund and organiser-cancellation terms are supplied before payment.
criteria.rationale: A participant needs to understand losses under each cancellation scenario.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Save the terms version accepted at payment.

criteria.criterion: Visa and work-authorisation responsibility is explicit.
criteria.rationale: A residency invitation does not determine immigration or work rights.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Check current official authority guidance for the participant’s nationality and activity.

criteria.criterion: Insurance expectations and exclusions are explicit.
criteria.rationale: Travel, health, equipment and cancellation risks may require different cover.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Record required cover and who bears uninsured costs.

criteria.criterion: Emergency contacts and evacuation procedures exist.
criteria.rationale: Shared accommodation in an unfamiliar place needs a practical incident plan.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Request emergency numbers, exits, assembly point and hospital route.

criteria.criterion: Health, accessibility and accommodation needs have a private route.
criteria.rationale: Participants need a way to discuss needs without public disclosure.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Test the confidential request and response process.

criteria.criterion: House rules cover guests, noise, substances and shared spaces.
criteria.rationale: Common expectations reduce avoidable conflict in a live-work house.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Review the cohort-specific house rules before acceptance.

criteria.criterion: Conflict, harassment and removal procedures are defined.
criteria.rationale: A community promise needs a safe route for complaints and proportionate action.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Record reporter options, decision owner and consequences.

criteria.criterion: Photography and public-content participation require separate agreement.
criteria.rationale: Joining a residency is not consent to marketing or documentary content.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Review release wording and the opt-out path.

criteria.criterion: Confidential projects and intellectual property remain under participant control.
criteria.rationale: Proximity should not force disclosure or transfer of project rights.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Review confidentiality and intellectual-property clauses.

criteria.criterion: The expected work rhythm and mandatory activities are stated.
criteria.rationale: A participant cannot assess fit without knowing the balance of focus and group time.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Record mandatory sessions, quiet hours and uninterrupted blocks.

criteria.criterion: Each participant controls their project and milestone.
criteria.rationale: Selection should not imply employment, investment or transfer of decision rights.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Review the agreement and milestone process.

criteria.criterion: Selection criteria and conflicts of interest are described.
criteria.rationale: Applicants should understand what is assessed and whether sponsors influence selection.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Record criteria, reviewers and material relationships.

criteria.criterion: Testimonials identify the cohort and have publication permission.
criteria.rationale: A quote without context or consent cannot establish a repeatable outcome.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Verify the speaker, cohort, approved wording and date.

criteria.criterion: Launch, revenue, funding and partnership claims link to a verifiable record.
criteria.rationale: Residency association should not be confused with causation or endorsement.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Request the public artifact and participant-approved attribution.

criteria.criterion: Outcomes state starting point, time horizon and limitations.
criteria.rationale: Without a baseline and timeframe, progress claims are easy to overread.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Record milestone, observed deliverable, later result and external factors.

criteria.criterion: Unresolved questions are listed before payment or travel.
criteria.rationale: A visible open-questions list prevents enthusiasm from becoming assumed fact.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Publish or retain a dated decision log with owner and due date.
